events.event: The earliest known patient with COVID-19 falls ill in Wuhan, China.
Wuhan reports a cluster of pneumonia cases of unknown cause to the World Health Organization.
The World Health Organization declares the outbreak a public health emergency of international concern.
The first two cases in the UK are confirmed, in York.
The first confirmed case among Cheltenham residents is recorded.
The first death in the UK of a patient with COVID-19 is confirmed.
The Cheltenham Festival begins, running for four days with crowds of more than 250,000 across the week.
The World Health Organization declares COVID-19 a pandemic.
The first national lockdown is announced: people must stay at home except for limited reasons.
Non-essential shops reopen in England.
Pubs, restaurants and hairdressers reopen in England.
The second national lockdown begins in England, lasting until 2 December.
The first COVID-19 vaccination in the UK is given, in Coventry.
The third national lockdown begins in England.
Non-essential shops, gyms, hairdressers and outdoor hospitality reopen in England.
Most legal restrictions end in England.
The first cases of the Omicron variant are confirmed in the UK.
The legal requirement to self-isolate after a positive test ends in England.
Free testing ends for most people in England, so far fewer cases are recorded from here on.
The World Health Organization declares that COVID-19 is no longer a global health emergency.
